Preview complete tables or select representative rows

Source: R/preview.R
special-print.Rd

Control how a complete table is printed, or select a smaller set of rows:

  • preview_table(): Keep the complete data and store a print preference. By default, show the first five and last five rows; interval previews show evenly spaced rows.

  • unpreview_table(): Remove the stored print preference, keeping all data.

  • print_headtail(): Print the first and last rows once, keeping all data.

  • print_interval(): Print evenly spaced rows once, keeping all data.

  • print_all(): Print every row and column, like Stata's list.

  • slice_headtail(): Return only the selected first and last rows.

  • slice_interval(): Return only the selected evenly spaced rows.

Usage

preview_table(.data, style = c("headtail", "interval"), n = 10)

unpreview_table(.data)

print_headtail(
  .data,
  n = 10,
  width = NULL,
  ...,
  max_extra_cols = NULL,
  max_footer_lines = NULL
)

print_all(.data, ..., width = Inf)

print_interval(
  .data,
  n = 10,
  width = NULL,
  ...,
  max_extra_cols = NULL,
  max_footer_lines = NULL
)

slice_headtail(.data, n = 10)

slice_interval(.data, n = 10)

Arguments

.data

An in-memory data frame, data.table, ordinary tibble, grouped tibble, rowwise tibble, or sf data frame (geometry is kept when slicing and printed as a column). Convert other subclasses explicitly before wrapping; collect lazy tables first. Apply the wrapper separately to lists of tables.

style

Either "headtail" or "interval".

n

Total number of rows to display or select: a positive whole number or Inf for all rows. An odd head/tail budget gives the head the extra row. With n = 1, both styles select the first row. Short tables do not repeat rows.

width

Console width, passed to tibble formatting. NULL uses the current console width; Inf (the default for print_all()) shows all columns.

...

Additional arguments passed to tibble formatting.

max_extra_cols, max_footer_lines

Tibble formatting controls.

Value

  • preview_table(): the complete input container with an additional tidystata_preview class and stored print settings.

  • unpreview_table(): the table without that class or its settings, preserving grouping.

  • Print helpers: the original input, invisibly.

  • Slice helpers: the selected rows in the input container, retaining valid grouping and existing preview settings. Explicit data.frame row names are preserved; automatic row names are regenerated as in dplyr slicing.

Supported containers are listed under .data; other subclasses are unsupported.

Details

Preview settings survive table subsetting/replacement, dplyr mutation, filtering, sorting, column selection, renaming, relocation, distinct rows, slicing, grouping, rowwise operations, summaries and reframing, as well as tidyr's pivot_longer() and pivot_wider(). Grouping follows the underlying operation. Joins inherit the left input's settings; bind_rows() inherits the first input's settings. Arbitrary third-party transformations and direct vctrs::vec_rbind() are not covered by this guarantee.

Positions shown in the margin refer to the current table, not the original data before filtering or sorting. Previewing does not change column values, classes, labels, or the data used in subsequent calculations. Grouped tables use a global row budget, not a separate budget per group.

print(x, n = Inf) displays the entire table. Per-call formatting overrides do not change stored settings. Explicit tibble::as_tibble() or as.data.frame() conversions remove the preview, as does column extraction. This feature controls console printing, not HTML widgets or GUI viewers. Only the temporary display is converted to a tibble. Wrapping and unwrapping a data.table creates an independent copy; native operations such as := on a wrapped data.table retain ordinary reference semantics. External dplyr/tidyr verbs determine their own result container and grouping, while preview settings follow the result.

See also

Other selection and preview functions: select_or_transmute(), varlist()

Examples

x <- preview_table(tibble::tibble(id = 1:30, value = (1:30)^2))
x
#> # A tibble: 30 x 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1     1     1
#>  2     2     4
#>  3     3     9
#>  4     4    16
#>  5     5    25
#> 26    26   676
#> 27    27   729
#> 28    28   784
#> 29    29   841
#> 30    30   900
#> # ... 20 rows omitted in the middle; use print(x, n = Inf) to show all rows.

dplyr::filter(x, id > 10)
#> # A tibble: 20 x 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
